title: Compatibility Gateway & Exit Corridor: Migration playbook for /generate v0 and longpoll transports
creator: Asha Patel
description: This ticket defines the Product Requirements Document and rollout playbook for introducing a Compatibility Gateway (adapter runtime) that transparently bridges remaining customers from deprecated /generate v0 synchronous and longpoll transports to the unified inference API. The gateway is intended as a temporary exit corridor to reduce client breakage while we accelerate client-side SDK migrations and telemetry gating.
background: Historically many customers integrated with /generate v0 and custom longpoll transports. After the unified inference API launch, adoption accelerated but a non-trivial portion of traffic (internal estimate ~6% of active orgs, skewed to enterprise) still depends on the old transports and model aliases. Complete, immediate removal would cause broad customer disruption. The Compatibility Gateway will offer protocol translation, rate-limited compatibility, and explicit migration hooks.
goals: Provide a time-boxed compatibility layer to preserve availability for customers unable to migrate immediately
Enable deterministic telemetry so we can measure migration progress and identify high-impact clients
Minimize the runtime and operational complexity by limiting gateway features and enforcing strict compatibility SLAs
Define clear acceptance and rollback criteria for each deprecation milestone
out_of_scope: Long-term indefinite support of v0 models or transports beyond the sunset window
Feature parity between the gateway and the unified API (we will implement a conservative subset only)
Custom on-prem gateway variants — private deployments should use private migration tooling instead
requirements: Compatibility Gateway must translate v0 request/response shapes to unified API equivalents for generate and streaming where feasible
Gateway must emit migration headers and a client-visible deprecation notice on first request per org per week
Gateway must support a per-org throttle and quota mapping so enterprise customers do not bypass reserved capacity policies
Gateway must provide precise telemetry labels (org_id, legacy_endpoint, models_in_use, first_seen_timestamp) exported to Console
Gateway feature must be enabled behind a rollout flag and default to disabled for new orgs
constraints_and_tradeoffs: We will not replicate server-sent-events multiplexing; the gateway will convert longpoll into short-lived streaming where possible, and fall back to synchronous responses with explicit truncation reasons
To limit maintenance burden, the gateway will accept only a curated set of model aliases deemed safe for transparent mapping
Strict rate limits will be applied to compatibility traffic to avoid negative impact on Dedicated capacity customers
acceptance_criteria: Compatibility Gateway is deployed to staging and passes synthetic traffic tests that validate shape translation for the curated alias set
Telemetry for legacy clients appears in Console dashboards with per-org migration progress and a baseline acceptance signal (>=95% mapping success for test corpus)
SDK and docs updated with explicit migration guide and opt-in flag; at least one major client library includes an example showing how to migrate polling to unified streaming
Rollout plan reviewed and signed off by Security, Sales Engineering, and Runtime teams
A rollback plan exists and has been smoke-tested (gateway can be disabled without service interruption within 15 minutes)
migration_strategy: Phase 0 (Prep, 2 weeks): finalize mapping table for aliases; dev build of gateway; create Console dashboards and examples
Phase 1 (Limited opt-in beta, 4 weeks): enable gateway for 5 pilot customers (Sales-assisted); collect telemetry and client feedback
Phase 2 (Controlled ramp, 6 weeks): enable gateway for broader cohort via opt-in in Console and SDK toggles; activate automated migration emails for org admins
Phase 3 (Sunset window start, 12 weeks): gateway becomes default for remaining eligible orgs with clear deadline notifications; begin enforcement of strict rate limits
Phase 4 (Sunset cutoff): disable gateway and remove v0 aliases after a final freeze and notice period (release milestone)
timeline: Start: 2025-03-17. Pilot start: 2025-03-31. Controlled ramp: 2025-04-28. Sunset window open: 2025-05-05. Sunset cutoff: 2025-07-05
monitoring_and_telemetry: Expose Console dashboard: legacy_traffic_by_org (real-time + 7d), mapping_success_rate, latency_p50/p95 for gateway path
Create alert: gateway_mapping_rate < 90% for 1h in production
Create alert: gateway_error_rate > 1% for 15m with org-level drilling
Instrument audit log entries for each translated request with correlation_id
rollback_criteria: If gateway introduction increases 99th percentile latency for unified API by >10% for 30m, pause rollout
If mapping_success_rate < 80% and error modes are not fixable in <48 hours, disable gateway for affected orgs
If there is an unanticipated customer-impact P0 incident attributable to gateway translation, roll back to previous routing rules immediately
communications_plan: Pre-announcement to Sales and Support with migration FAQ and playbook
Email sequence to affected org admins: notice -> migration tips -> final deadline (30/14/7/1 days)
Console banners for affected orgs and in-SDK deprecation warnings
Public changelog entry with timeline and link to migration guide
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Customers with customized SDKs won't see Console banners — Mitigation: Sales-assisted outreach and host a migration clinic
Risk: Gateway could mask broken client behavior and delay proper fixes — Mitigation: Telemetry to identify persistent clients and require fix plans after 6 weeks
Risk: Dedicated capacity customers could be impacted by uncontrolled compatibility traffic — Mitigation: per-org throttle mapping and opt-out capability for Dedicated contracts
implementation_notes: Gateway will be implemented as a lightweight stateless service in the routing plane, with translations applied via a single versioned mapping table
Runtime team to ship a feature flag that routes a percentage of traffic to gateway for canarying
Dev QA to include replay tests using anonymized real legacy traffic traces (privacy-approved)
